## Castel Bolognese, Ravenna, Emilia-Romagna, Italy — Locality Guide (1850–1870)

### Jurisdictional Context
Castel Bolognese was part of the **Papal States** until 1860, when it joined the Kingdom of Sardinia; it became part of the unified **Kingdom of Italy** in 1861. This transition is the single most important fact for record availability in this period: **civil (stato civile) registration did not exist** in Castel Bolognese between 1816 and 1865. A birth in 1860 was recorded only in the Catholic parish baptismal register (*battesimi*).

### Record Regimes, 1850–1870

#### Pre-1866 (1850–1865): Ecclesiastical Records Only
- **Primary source**: Catholic parish baptismal register (*battesimi*) kept by the local parish church in Castel Bolognese, under the Diocese of Imola.
- **FamilySearch availability**: NONE found. No parish register volumes for Castel Bolognese appeared in volume_search for this period. The FamilySearch wiki page section for 'Church Records' for Castel Bolognese is empty.
- **Where to look**: Diocesan Archive of Imola (*Archivio Diocesano di Imola*) or the local parish directly. Antenati does NOT cover this period.
- **Napoleonic gap note**: Napoleonic civil registration (1806–1815) is available as browse-only images at FamilySearch Catalog (catalog 3026019, held at Archivio di Stato di Bologna, sez. Imola) — but this does not extend to 1860.

#### Post-1866: Civil Registration — Well Digitized
- **Italy, Ravenna, Ravenna, Civil Registration (Tribunale), 1866–1943** (FS collection 1947700) — **indexed & images**.
  - Nati (births): 1866–1870 volumes all at **100% record-searchable** (name-indexed). Searchable via `record_search`.
  - Matrimoni (marriages): 1866–1870 at 100% indexed.
  - Morti (deaths): 1866–1870 at 60–86% indexed.
- **Registri dello stato civile di Castel Bolognese (Ravenna) 1866–1929** (catalog 1315917) — images only.
- **Italia, Ravenna, Castel Bolognese. Stato civile, Tribunale: 1869–1945** (catalog 2519721) — images.
- **Antenati** (antenati.cultura.gov.it): civil registration images and indexes from 1866; search by location for Castel Bolognese.

#### Allegati (Supporting Documents)
Marriage and birth supporting document bundles (*allegati*) for 1866–1867 are digitized but largely browse-only (some full-text searchable). The 1866 *allegati matrimoni* (M93F-TBK) is **full-text searchable**. These bundles may contain baptismal extracts (*estratti di battesimo*) for children born before 1866 when they later married.

#### Decennial Indexes (Indici Decennali)
Browse-only name indexes for births, deaths, and marriages 1866–1875 exist (image groups 007847845_054, _064, _059) but are not name-indexed or full-text searchable.

### External Resources
- **Antenati** (antenati.cultura.gov.it) — Italian National Archives civil registration portal, 1866+
- **Italy Births and Baptisms 1806–1900** (FS collection 1708706 / MyHeritage) — may include church-extracted baptism records
- **italianparishrecords.org** — external index of Italian parish records
- **FamilySearch Research Guide for Italy** (BYU PDF) — covers ecclesiastical record strategy

### Key Research Strategy Note
For a birth **circa 1860** in Castel Bolognese: the direct record (baptismal register) is not currently online. The practical research path is: (1) search the 1866–1870 indexed civil births for any Mingazzini births listing Sebastiano and Lucia as parents — this establishes the family corpus and may bracket the gap; (2) search marriage allegati for older Mingazzini children marrying after 1866, whose supporting documents may include a baptismal extract for a c. 1860 birth; (3) for a definitive answer on a pre-1866 birth, the Diocesan Archive of Imola must be consulted directly.

Under the Italian *Codice Civile* of 1865, parties to a civil marriage proceeding were legally required to declare their parentage under oath to the registrar (*ufficiale dello stato civile*), and the allegati (supporting documents) typically included a baptismal extract. The groom's declaration of parentage was therefore both legally sworn and subject to registrar verification — though the underlying allegato was not examined.
